title: Meta ran hundreds of ads with AI-generated child abuse imagery
summary: The Tech Transparency Project reported that Meta failed to detect 332 ads containing AI-generated child sexual abuse material, many promoting nudify apps.
note: Counts against C8 for Facebook and Instagram.

title: ISD maps the nudify tools ecosystem
summary: The Institute for Strategic Dialogue found mainstream platforms sent millions of users to nudify apps between Dec 2025 and Mar 2026, with YouTube, X, Reddit and Facebook as the main sources.
note: Counts against C8 for YouTube, X, Reddit and Facebook.

title: Thousands of nudify-app ads on Facebook and Instagram
summary: A Tech Transparency Project report found more than 7,600 ads for apps built to produce non-consensual imagery of women, placed through one advertising partner.
note: Counts against C8 for Facebook and Instagram.

title: Government report flags harassment and abuse content on Telegram
summary: A June 2026 Indian government report reviewed by Reuters said Telegram channels were reported by citizens for online harassment and child sexual abuse content.

title: Delhi High Court upholds temporary Telegram block
summary: India blocked Telegram until 22 June 2026 over leaked NEET-UG exam papers, and the Delhi High Court upheld the block.

title: IT Rules amendment cuts NCII takedown to 2 hours
summary: MeitY introduced amendments, in force 20 Feb 2026: NCII and morphed images must come down within 2 hours, AI content must be labelled, and court or government orders must be met within 3 hours.
note: Law change, not a platform failure.

title: Ofcom opens formal investigation into X over Grok images
summary: The UK regulator opened an Online Safety Act investigation after reports that Grok was used to create and share undressed images of people.

title: MeitY notice to X over Grok 'undressing' images
summary: MeitY issued a notice on 2 January 2026; X removed about 3,500 posts and 600 accounts.

title: MeitY issues the NCII Standard Operating Procedure
summary: Issued after a Madras High Court order, the SOP lists reporting routes and requires large platforms to use hash-matching and crawlers.
note: Policy change, not a platform failure.
